translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus our hope,
to Timothy, a beloved son in the faith: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.
As I urged you to remain in Ephesus when I was going to Macedonia, so that you might command certain people not to teach different doctrines,
and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which stir up disputes rather than further God's work through faith.
For the aim of the command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith.
Some have strayed from these and turned aside to empty talk.
They want to be teachers of the law, but they themselves understand neither what they are saying nor the things they so firmly assert.
We know that the law is good if someone uses it lawfully.

But let that person understand this: the law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the lawless and disobedient, the ungodly and sinful, the unholy and profane, those who dishonor their fathers and mothers, murderers,
the sexually immoral, men who have sexual relations with men, kidnappers, liars, those who swear falsely, and anything else that is contrary to sound teaching,
which accords with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I was entrusted.
I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who strengthened me, because he considered me faithful and appointed me to service.
Although I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an abuser, I received mercy because I acted in ignorance and unbelief.
And the grace of our Lord overflowed, along with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
This saying is trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost.
But I received mercy for this reason: so that Jesus Christ might first show all his patience in me, as an example to those who would believe in him for eternal life.
Now to the King of the ages, incorruptible and invisible, the only God, be glory and honor forever and ever. Amen.
I entrust this command to you, my child Timothy, in accordance with the prophecies previously made about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight.
Hold to faith with a pure mind; some have rejected this and have been shipwrecked in the faith.
Among these are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that they might be taught not to blaspheme.
And now, before everything else, I urge that prayers, requests, supplications, and thanksgivings be offered for all people,
especially for kings and all rulers, so that we may lead our lives peacefully and quietly, in all godliness and holiness.
For this is good and acceptable before God our Savior,
who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God and one mediator between God and humanity, the man Jesus Christ,
who gave himself as a ransom for all, a testimony at the appointed times.
For this I was appointed a preacher and an apostle—I speak the truth in Christ and do not lie—and became a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
I want men to pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands without anger or doubt.
Likewise, women should adorn themselves modestly, with reverence and self-control, not with golden braids interwoven with pearls or with ornate clothing,
but with good works, as is fitting for women who profess devotion to God.
Let a woman learn quietly, with complete submission.
But I do not permit a woman to teach a man or to speak arrogantly over a man, but to remain silent.
For Adam was created first, and then Eve.
And Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and transgressed.
But she will be saved through childbearing, if they remain in faith and love and holiness, with self-control.
This saying is trustworthy: if anyone desires to be a bishop, he desires a good work.
A bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, gentle, humble, respectable, hospitable, and able to teach.
Not abusive, not violent, but gentle; not quarrelsome, not a lover of money.
He must manage his own household well and have children who remain obedient with all dignity.
But if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for the church of God?
He must not be a new convert, lest he become proud and fall under the condemnation of Satan.
He must also have a good reputation among outsiders, lest he fall into disgrace and Satan’s snare.
Likewise, deacons must be respectable, not double-tongued, not fond of wine, and not greedy for dishonest gain,
but must hold the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience.
Let them first be tested, and then enter into service, provided they are blameless.
Likewise, their wives must be respectable, not slanderers, gentle, and faithful in everything.
Deacons must be husbands of one wife, managing their own children and households well.
For those who serve well gain a good standing for themselves and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
I write this to you because I hope to come soon.
But if I delay, so that you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

And clearly, great is the mystery of devotion to God: he who appeared in the flesh was vindicated by the Spirit, revealed to angels, preached among the Gentiles, believed in throughout the world, and taken up in glory.
But the Holy Spirit plainly says that in later times some will depart from the faith and turn their attention to spirits of deception and teachings of demons,
through the hypocrisy of liars whose own consciences are seared,
who forbid marriage and abstain from foods that God established for believers and those who have come to know the truth to enjoy.
For everything God created is good, and nothing is to be rejected, especially when it is received with thanksgiving,
for it is made holy by the word of God and by prayers.
By giving this instruction to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and the good teaching that you have followed.
But reject profane talk and old women's tales, and train yourself in godliness.
For bodily training is useful to a small extent, but godliness is useful in every way and holds the promise of life, both now and in the world to come.
This saying is trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance.
For this very purpose we labor and endure insults, because we have placed our hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of believers.
Command and teach these things.
Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to believers in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity.
Until I come, devote yourself to reading, exhortation, and teaching.
Do not neglect the gift within you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of hands by the elders.
Reflect on these things and devote yourself to them, so that your progress may be evident to everyone.
Pay close attention to yourself and your teaching, and persevere in this. If you do so, you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.
Do not rebuke an older man harshly, but appeal to him as to a father, and to younger men as to brothers.
Treat older women as mothers and younger women as sisters, with complete purity.
Honor widows who are truly widows.
But if a widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to do good to their own households and repay their parents, for this is good and acceptable before God.
But a woman who is truly a widow and left alone has placed her hope in God and devotes herself to prayers and petitions night and day.
But a widow who lives in luxury is dead even while she lives.
Command these things so that they may be blameless.
But if anyone does not care for his own people, especially the members of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let a widow be enrolled among the widows only if she is at least sixty years old and has been the wife of one husband.
She must also be known for good works: whether she has raised children, welcomed strangers, washed the feet of the saints, helped those in distress, and pursued every good work.
But refuse younger widows, for when their desires lead them away from Christ, they want to marry.
They bring judgment upon themselves because they have disregarded their first pledge.
At the same time, they learn to be idle, going from house to house, and not only idle but also gossips and busybodies, saying things they should not.
So I want younger women to marry, bear children, manage their households, and give the adversary no occasion for slander.
For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
If any believer has widows in his care, let him provide for them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it can provide for those who are truly widows.
Let the elders who oversee well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching.
For Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing,” and, “The worker deserves his wages.”
Do not accept an accusation against an elder except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
Rebuke those who sin before everyone, so that the others too may be afraid.
I charge you before God and Jesus Christ and the chosen angels to observe these things without prejudgment, doing nothing out of partiality.
Do not be quick to lay hands on anyone, and do not share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
From now on, do not drink only water, but mix in a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
Some people's sins are evident and reach judgment ahead of them, while the sins of others follow after them.
Likewise, good works are evident, and even those that are otherwise cannot remain hidden.
Let all who are under the yoke of slavery consider their own masters worthy of honor, so that God's name and the teaching may not be blasphemed.

Those who have believing masters must not despise them because they are brothers. Rather, they must serve them all the more, because those who benefit from their service are believers and beloved. Teach these things and encourage them.
But if anyone teaches something different and does not heed the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and the teaching that accords with godliness,
such a person is puffed up and knows nothing, but is consumed with disputes and arguments over words, from which come envy, strife, blasphemies, and evil suspicions,
and the deceitful dealings of people whose minds are corrupted and who are estranged from the truth, who consider godliness a means of profit. But you must withdraw from such people.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out.
But we have food and clothing, and let us be content with these.
But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge people into destruction and ruin.
For the love of money is the root of all evils. Some, longing for it, have strayed from the faith and subjected themselves to many pains.
But you, O man of God, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith and take hold of eternal life, to which you were called and for which you made the good confession before many witnesses.
I command you before God, who gives life to everything, and Jesus Christ, who testified to the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
to keep the commandment spotless and blameless until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
which the blessed and only mighty One, the King of kings and Lord of lords, will reveal at the appointed times,
who alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no human being has seen or can see. To him be honor and power forever. Amen.
Command those who are rich in this world not to be proud and not to put their hope in empty wealth, but in God, who gives us everything abundantly to enjoy.
Tell them to do good, to be rich in good deeds, to be generous, loving, and ready to share,
storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of true life.
O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you, turning away from profane and novel talk, from disputes, and from falsely named knowledge,
which some have professed and thereby strayed from the faith. Grace be with you. The first letter to Timothy was written from Laodicea, which is the capital of the Pacatians.
